1 λέγει? at cf. l. 3. 2 ἀνοικτῶ (οι dubium) cod. φωτεινῶ cod. 3 δημοσία cod.
4 συμμπαροὺς τούτους cod. 6 lac. sign. Kroll. 13 μεσήλικα cod. 18-19 εἰ δὲ μέτα
ζ τῆς κλεπ’ 66 cod., εἰ δὲ μετὰ ζ’ τῆς κλοπῆς ἡμέρας dubitanter scripsi. 20 καὶ
seclusi, τι coni. Kroll. πείσεται scripsi, πήσεται cod. κλήρου scripsi, κλεπ’ cod.
22 με γέγονεν cod., μὴ γεγονέναι dub. scripsi. 23 οὐ ἡ ante λέγε cod., lac. signavi,
οὗ οἱ λ. Kroll. κατὰ suppl. Kroll. 27 βλέπουσι cod. δυσεύρεται cod., -τον scripsi.
28 θέλη cod., corr. Kroll. 31 δεξαμένην cod. 33 δεῖοσθαι <sic> cod., δεδόσθαι

sections.en: 1 λέγει ('he says')? but compare l. 3. 2 ἀνοικτῶ ('open') (οι doubtful) the codex has. φωτεινῶ ('bright') the codex has. 3 δημοσία ('public') the codex has. 4 συμμπαροὺς τούτους ('these companions') the codex has. 6 lacuna indicated by Kroll. 13 μεσήλικα ('middle-aged') the codex has. 18-19 εἰ δὲ μέτα ζ τῆς κλεπ’ 66 ('but if after 7 of the theft 66') the codex has, εἰ δὲ μετὰ ζ’ τῆς κλοπῆς ἡμέρας ('but if after 7 days of the theft') I have written hesitantly. 20 καὶ ('and') bracketed by me, τι ('something') conjectured by Kroll. πείσεται ('will suffer') I have written, πήσεται ('will suffer') the codex has. κλήρου ('of the lot') I have written, κλεπ’ ('theft') the codex has. 22 με γέγονεν ('has happened to me') the codex has, μὴ γεγονέναι ('not to have happened') I have written hesitantly. 23 οὐ ἡ ('not the') before λέγε ('say') the codex has, I have indicated a lacuna, οὗ οἱ λ. ('where the say') Kroll. κατὰ ('according to') supplied by Kroll. 27 βλέπουσι ('they see') the codex has. δυσεύρεται ('hard to find') the codex has, -τον ('hard to find') I have written. 28 θέλη ('he may wish') the codex has, corrected by Kroll. 31 δεξαμένην ('having received') the codex has. 33 δεῖοσθαι ('to need') <sic> the codex has, δεδόσθαι ('to have been given') corrected by Kroll. Or δεῖσθαι ('to need')? 34 ἐστὶν ('is') the codex has. ὦσιν ('they may be') I have written but compare 8. 35 βαρεῖ ('heavy') the codex has.

summary.headline: Rules for Lost Things and Thieves
summary.text: Astrological rules for identifying thieves and locating lost objects through the Sun, Moon, planets, lots, signs, houses, exaltations, depressions, and planetary phases. The text assigns thieves’ status, age, appearance, fate, and likely hiding places such as wells, woods, mountains, offices, smithies, kitchens, and dark or elevated places.
